punchline: In the writers' room of The Simpsons, it does not matter whose joke it was; the credits show the team's name.
thirty_sec: Adam Grant argues that creative teams feed on a generous culture, and uses the writers' room of The Simpsons as his example. Dozens of writers produce jokes for hours. One throws out a gag, another builds on it, a third ties it to a better ending. Nobody says "that one was mine". Not caring about credit frees the total intelligence of the team.
